title: Commissioning: level reads high near empty
summary: Both level measurements should agree, but LT-203 reads clearly higher, most of all when the tank is nearly empty. Check the analog configuration against the drawing.
objectives: Calculate the expected current for a level
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed: TRUE while not pressed. *)
    LevelHigh : BOOL; (* High level switch LSH-205: TRUE when wet. *)
    InletOpen : BOOL; (* Inlet valve open limit switch. *)
    LevelRaw : INT; (* LT-203, 4-20 mA: generic profile 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
    CheckRaw : INT; (* LT-204, 0-10 V cross-check: generic profile 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-201 solenoid. *)
    DrainPump : BOOL; (* Drain pump P-202. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level from LT-203, 0..100 %. *)
    CheckPercent : REAL; (* Level from LT-204, 0..100 %. *)
    DeviationAlarm : BOOL; (* The two measurements differ by more than 5 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Filling : BOOL; (* Fill request latch. *)
END_VAR
(* The program passed its factory test; this lab is about the installation and configuration. *)
LevelPercent := INT_TO_REAL(LevelRaw) / 100.0;
CheckPercent := INT_TO_REAL(CheckRaw) / 100.0;
DeviationAlarm := (LevelPercent - CheckPercent > 5.0) OR (CheckPercent - LevelPercent > 5.0);
Filling := (StartPB OR Filling) AND StopPB AND NOT LevelHigh AND NOT DeviationAlarm AND LevelPercent < 80.0;
InletValve := Filling;
DrainPump := FALSE;
END_PROGRAM
instructions: The PLC runs the accepted program. Press Start and confirm the symptom.
Open the Commissioning tab: work through the analog checks against the drawing.
Measure the loop current or voltage at the analog input and compare it with the sight glass.
hints: At 20 % level a 4-20 mA transmitter delivers 7.2 mA.
What does a 0-20 mA input make of 7.2 mA?

scenarios.title: Start filling and let the tank reach its setpoint

criteria.title: Both measurements agree with the tank level
criteria.onFail: LevelPercent and CheckPercent were not about 20 % while the tank held 20 %.

criteria.title: No deviation alarm while filling
criteria.onFail: The two level measurements disagreed by more than 5 %.

troubleshooting.symptom: The tank does not fill: the deviation alarm is active, and LT-203 reads higher than LT-204.

diagnosisOptions.label: The PLC program scales the levels wrongly
The LT-203 current loop is broken
The LT-203 input does not supply the 2-wire loop
The LT-204 input is configured for current instead of 0-10 V
The LT-203 input is configured for 0-20 mA instead of 4-20 mA
LT-203 reads too high: its zero is offset
The inlet valve does not open

debrief.rootCause: The LT-203 input was configured for 0-20 mA while the transmitter delivers 4-20 mA. The input treated the 4 mA live zero as 20 %, so LT-203 read too high, most of all near empty, and the deviation alarm blocked filling.
evidence: At 20 % level the loop measured 7.2 mA, the correct 4-20 mA value.
The channel was configured for 0-20 mA, so 7.2 mA became 36 %.
LT-204 and the sight glass showed 20 %.
debrief.repair: Configure the LT-203 input for 4-20 mA and download the configuration.
debrief.reasoning: A constant offset that shrinks towards full scale is typical for a 0-20 mA versus 4-20 mA mismatch. Calculate the expected current for a known level and compare it with the measurement.
